title: Arc Left
description: An arc left is a curved dolly that travels partway around the subject while staying aimed at them. The camera's axis on the conversation or room changes without a cut, usually about a quarter-orbit.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: You change who owns the background. A three-quarter face can become a profile, a window can replace a wall, the other half of a room can arrive.
The subject stays the center; the world slides. It is the wrong tool when you needed a full spin, a straight truck, or a pan from sticks.
If radius collapses, you accidentally pushed in.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Lay a curved track or walk a measured radius, always facing the figure. Keep distance roughly constant.
Ninety degrees is enough for most coverage. Prompt a 90-degree arc left around the subject, curved dolly, always facing the figure, background sliding.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it to change the axis of a conversation or reveal the other half of a room. Concrete beat: from a frontal two-shot into a profile that discloses a listener in the doorway.
Do not complete 360 unless spectacle is the job.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: 360-Degree Orbit finishes the circle. Arc Right is the other direction: pick the side that produces the new wall.
A Dolly Left is linear, not curved, so distance to the subject will change unless they also move. Arc left is a partial azimuth on a radius.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Goodfellas uses curved approaches as social weather, distinct from its straight Copa track. Atonement's long beach and house passages include arcing camera to re-axis crowds and rooms.
Take the quarter-turn, not the whole set-piece.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a Dolly Left or a full 360-Degree Orbit. The tell is a straight track that loses the subject, or a spin that never stops.
The fix: curved path, constant radius, about 90 degrees, lens on the person.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Arc Left in film?
It is a partial leftward orbit: the camera travels a curve around a subject while remaining aimed at them, changing background and face angle.
Arc Left vs 360-Degree Orbit
A 360 orbit completes the circle and often becomes the event. Arc left is a coverage curve, usually about 90 degrees, to change axis.
When should I use Arc Left?
When a conversation or a room needs a new axis without a cut. Do not use a full orbit for that job.
How do I prompt Arc Left for AI image or video?
Write 90-degree arc left, curved dolly, always facing [Subject], constant distance, background sliding. Ban a full 360 unless you change technique.
